tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (connection errors, timeouts, alarms firing) rather than implementation details, explicitly enumerates trigger contexts (specific error replies, metrics, scenarios) including cases where the user may not name the domain directly ('Use it even if only the symptom is described'), and also clearly states out-of-scope cases. It is a single dense paragraph which is reasonably concise given the breadth of triggers it needs to cover.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an application that uses an Amazon ElastiCache cache (node-based or serverless; Valkey, Redis OSS or Memcached) sees connection errors or timeouts, command errors or timeouts... Use it even if only the symptom is described. Do not use it to create, size or migrate caches, or for self-managed Valkey or Redis (for example on EC2).

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with domain-specific rules, non-obvious edge cases, and procedures specific to ElastiCache troubleshooting. It never explains general concepts like what caching or CloudWatch are; it jumps straight into ElastiCache-specific scope, rules, and workflow.
tests.evidence: G1: use the classic metric where OpenTelemetry has no equivalent. That is CurrItems, CurrVolatileItems, latency percentiles, ReplicationLag...

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (metric lists, error reply tables, mitigation rows) is kept in references/ files and only summarized or pointed to in the body. The rules (G1-G4) are concise constraints, not data dumps.
tests.evidence: Load [references/error-replies.md](references/error-replies.md) to map it to its cause.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ has a corresponding markdown link in the SKILL.md body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a clear condition specifying when to load it (e.g., check engine version, during Step 1/2, when an error reply appears, when operator asks for mitigation).
tests.evidence: When the operator quotes an engine error reply, or the error metrics show one, load [references/error-replies.md](references/error-replies.md) to map it to its cause.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at 'references/' with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (mitigation application, read-only investigation rules) are given exact, prescriptive steps, while judgment-heavy tasks (judging causes, ruling out lookalikes) are described with reasoning and explanation of purpose rather than rigid steps.
tests.evidence: Mark each cause confirmed... ruled out... or unknown... The cause is confirmed only when its evidence is present and the lookalike's evidence is absent.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple metric paths exist (OpenTelemetry vs classic), the skill gives a clear rule for which to use by default and when to fall back to the other, rather than presenting them as equal options.
tests.evidence: G1: use the classic metric where OpenTelemetry has no equivalent... For node-based Valkey, query both paths.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable investigative method (identify deployment, collect evidence, judge causes, validate, report, mitigate) applicable to any ElastiCache incident, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Name the root cause of an ElastiCache incident from evidence, rule out the lookalike cause that produces the same symptom, and give the operator a fix.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The Rules section (G1-G4) functions as a gotchas section, documenting non-obvious environment-specific pitfalls like metric path gaps, data-loss fixes, and capacity-change mistakes.
tests.evidence: G4: never recommend a capacity change (a larger node, more shards or replicas, higher serverless limits) for a hot key, an unbounded collection or a client-side cause.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill specifies a clear 5-part report structure for output, which serves as the template for the structured output it produces.
tests.evidence: Always give all five parts, even when the cause looks obvious. 1. Root cause... 2. Evidence... 3. Ruled out... 4. Remediation... 5. Gaps...

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The report template in Step 5 is short (5 bullet items, well under 20 lines) and appropriately kept inline.
tests.evidence:
1. Root cause: one sentence naming the mechanism, not the symptom.
2. Evidence: metric, node/shard, value and time, against the baseline.
